q: Given only a natural-language specification and an empty workspace, an agent must implement a complete, installable project
r: Include: new benchmark of whole-repository generation from natural-language specs, 13 models with 4 runs each.

q: coding agents now able to produce functionally correct software projects from natural language prompts
r: Include: evaluates coding agents on project generation with a new three-layer dependency metric framework and repeated protocol (evaluation-method contribution).

q: ParanoiaEval is the first unified benchmark of coding agents’ risk-treatment capability
r: Include: new benchmark and judge for repository-level coding tasks, 3 runs per configuration, human study; contribution is the evaluation method.

q: an automated framework that audits the successes reported by coding benchmarks by evolving the evaluator
r: EC6: audits patch correctness on mostly SWE-bench-style issue-repair benchmarks; test-adequacy auditing rather than code development.

q: PolyCodeEval, a unified multilingual and multi-granularity benchmark for code generation
r: Include: new benchmark including complete-repository generation, compares LLMs, specialised methods and coding agents with cost metrics.

q: We introduce SWE-DUEL, a self-scaling arena that evaluates coding agents with each other
r: Include: new evaluation method (self-scaling tournament, Bradley-Terry ratings) where agents implement features and fix bugs in real repositories.

q: Agents iteratively modify a persistent codebase
r: Include: new benchmark of cumulative feature requests extending web applications, with new metrics.

q: We introduce two metrics for reporting results
r: Include: main contribution is an evaluation framework (paired interventions, cost metrics, repeated runs, controlled comparison of agents, harnesses, skills); HPC domain exception (ii) applies.

q: asks it to construct a complete candidate harness inside an isolated container
r: Include: new benchmark where models build a complete software project from a development document and contract skeleton, tested with hundreds of cases.

q: We introduce Graph Credit, a deterministic, test-grounded metric
r: Include: new benchmark and metric for multi-PR feature-level repository tasks; evaluation-method contribution.
